sub: Group-II S1-93: Later reorganisation of states and the creation of new states up to 2014
Group-II M1-A-109: Telangana agitation of 1969 - causes, course and outcome
Group-II M1-A-110: Jai Andhra movement of 1972 and the Six-Point Formula 1973
Group-II M1-A-111: Mulki rules, GO 610 and the implementation of safeguards
Group-II M1-A-120: Movement for a separate Telangana (1990s-2014) and the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act 2014

secs.t: Articles 2, 3, 4 and 368 → provisions on new states

x: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and to increase or diminish the area, alter the boundaries, or change the name of any State.
A law under Article 3 requires only
a simple majority
in Parliament and is not a constitutional amendment under Article 368 by virtue of Article 4.
The time limit for the affected State Legislature to express its views on an Article 3 Bill was added by the
5th Amendment, 1955

secs.t: New states and UTs → year and law (1960-2019) — State → year → law

x: The
Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat movements
led to the division of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.
The 1966 reorganisation divided Punjab into Punjab and Haryana, while Chandigarh was made a Union Territory and served as their shared capital.
Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became states in 1972 under the
North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971

secs.t: New states and UTs → year and law (1960-2019) — FIRSTs and traps

x: Exam angle: ascending-order questions - AP (1953/56) → Haryana (1966) → Chhattisgarh (2000) → Telangana (2014).
Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand
were created in 2000, with regional backwardness being an important consideration rather than linguistic identity.
The former State Legislature and its Legislative Council were abolished, and Jammu and Kashmir now has a Legislative Assembly as a Union Territory.

secs.t: Bases of state formation → states; pending statehood demands

x: The sequence is 1907 demand, 1980 foundation of the GNLF and coinage of ‘Gorkhaland’, 1988 formation of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council, and 2011 formation of the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration.

Andhra (1953) was the first linguistic State; Meghalaya (like Nagaland, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh) was formed on an ethnic/tribal basis; Uttarakhand (like Telangana) on regional backwardness/administrative grounds.

secs.t: Mulki rules — origin, definition and chronology 1888-2014 — Origin and FIRST

x: The Mulki rules originated in
Hyderabad State in 1888
, during the rivalry between Mulki and non-Mulki groups in the Nizam's bureaucracy.
The 1919 Farman required outsiders to obtain the Nizam's personal permission, strengthening the protection of local employment.
The Nizam's rules used a 15-year continuous residence requirement, while the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement suggested domicile rules such as 12 years' residence.

secs.t: Mulki rules — origin, definition and chronology 1888-2014 — Chronology → event → stance

x: The 1969 Jai Telangana agitation was centred in Telangana and demanded implementation of Mulki safeguards along with a separate State.
The correct sequence is Jai Telangana agitation (1969), Jai Andhra agitation (1972), 32nd Amendment (1973), GO 610 (1985), and Girglani Report (2004).
The Six-Point Formula of 1973 and the 32nd Amendment represented a compromise after the regional agitations concerning Mulki safeguards.

secs.t: Jai Telangana 1969 → causes, start and police firings

x: Non-locals were alleged to have been recruited, Telangana’s revenue surplus was allegedly diverted, and the political safeguards were considered unenforceable in court.
The regional sub-committee was extended in 1968; the first hunger strike occurred in January 1969; the TPS was formed in February 1969; and the agitation intensified by March 1969.
Severe police firings during the 1969 movement resulted in the death of
over 360
students and agitators, remembered as the Telangana martyrs.

secs.t: Parties and persons → role in the 1969 and 1972 agitations — Telangana Praja Samiti - founder, year, election, merger

x: The 1969 Jai Telangana agitation was led by the
Telangana Praja Samithi
, with A. Madan Mohan as its convener.
The Telangana Praja Samiti won 10 of the 14 Lok Sabha seats it contested in Telangana in the 1971 election.
Those who opposed the merger of the Telangana Praja Samiti with the Congress formed the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.

secs.t: Parties and persons → role in the 1969 and 1972 agitations — Chief Ministers → period and role

x: Exam angle: CM in 1969 = Kasu Brahmananda Reddy; CM in Jai Andhra 1972 = P.V. Narasimha Rao. Examiners pair these two.
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy was CM in 1969 and was forced to resign by the agitation; P.V. Narasimha Rao was sworn in on 30 September 1971 and was CM during Jai Andhra.

secs.t: Formulas 1969-1973 → date, clauses and committees — Eight-Point Formula (11 April 1969)

x: The Eight-Point Formula was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi at a special meeting in Delhi on
11 April 1969

The Bhargava Committee assessed Telangana's revenue surpluses, the Lalit Committee undertook official accounting of surplus funds, and the Wanchoo Committee examined the constitutional validity of job safeguards.
Clause 8 of the Eight-Point Formula provided that the Prime Minister would review progress every
six months
with central ministers and the Planning Commission Vice-Chairman.

secs.t: Formulas 1969-1973 → date, clauses and committees — Five-Point Formula - two versions

x: The Eight-Point Formula was announced by Indira Gandhi on 11 April 1969 during the Jai Telangana agitation, while the Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 belongs to the Jai Andhra phase.
The Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 brought Assistant Surgeons and Assistant Engineers under the Mulki rules, adding fuel to the
Jai Andhra agitation
that had followed the October 1972 Supreme Court judgment upholding the Mulki Rules.

secs.t: Formulas 1969-1973 → date, clauses and committees — Six-Point Formula (1973)

x: Exam angle: amendment number (32nd), date of President's Rule (Jan 1973), and which article gave the Central University (371E).
The third point of the Six-Point Formula provided for a committee to settle government employees’ grievances.
Backward-area development was to be addressed through
a State Planning Commission with local sub-committees
Article 371E provides for the establishment of
a Central University at Hyderabad

secs.t: Court verdicts on Mulki rules → case, year, effect

x: In A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court struck down the Telangana residence requirement in the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957, invoking Article 16(3).
The October 1972 ruling concerned the older Mulki Rules; the residence clause of the 1957 Act had been struck down in A.V.S. Narasimha Rao in 1969.
The correct sequence is 1957 Act, 1969 A.V.S. Narasimha Rao judgment, October 1972 judgment upholding the Mulki Rules, and 1973 repeal under the Six-Point Formula.
The Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula and replaced by the
zonal system

secs.t: Jai Andhra 1972-73 → cause, escalation, President's Rule, end

x: The movement was a counter-agitation in Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema, followed the October 1972 judgment, and saw the hoisting of a separate Andhra State flag on 10 December 1972.
The separate Andhra flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972; P. V. Narasimha Rao resigned and President's Rule began on 18 January 1973.
After P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned on 18 January 1973 amid a breakdown of law and order during Jai Andhra, President's Rule lasted until 10 December 1973 - the first in AP since the State was formed.

secs.t: 32nd Amendment 1973 → Articles 371D and 371E

x: Exam angle: APHQ 2019 asked which amendment brought in the Six-Point Formula - the
32nd
Article 371D provided for an Administrative Tribunal for service disputes, taking them out of the High Court's jurisdiction.
The Act continued the existing admission quotas under Article 371D for ten years and extended the operation of Article 371D to Telangana.
The 32nd Amendment Act, 1973 inserted
Articles 371D and 371E
to provide constitutional backing for the Six-Point Formula.

secs.t: Presidential Order 1975 → zones and local cadres

x: Local cadres could be organised district-wise, zone-wise or multi-zone-wise, and direct recruitment was reserved for locals of the relevant area.
After 2014, Andhra Pradesh retained
Zones I to IV
for its 13 districts; Zones V and VI related to the Telangana region.

Zone I consisted of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam; Zone II of East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone III of Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore; and Zone IV of Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.

secs.t: GO 610 (1985) and Girglani Commission (2001-04) → issued by, purpose, findings

x: GO 610 sought to repatriate non-local employees appointed contrary to the 1975 Presidential Order and restore local posts to Telangana candidates.
The commission headed by J.M. Girglani examined violations and highlighted large-scale non-local appointments in Telangana zones, particularly Zone VI.
GO 610
was weakly implemented, leading to the constitution of the Girglani Commission to examine continuing violations of the Presidential Order and GO 610.

secs.t: Separate Telangana movement 1969-2014 → event and year

x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001, the Centre's announcement followed in December 2009, the Srikrishna Committee report came in December 2010, and the Million March occurred in March 2011.
The Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana was adopted in July 2013, later than the TRS formation in 2001, the Srikrishna Committee report in 2010 and Sakala Janula Samme in 2011.

secs.t: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 → dates and Parts — Step → date

x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 18 February 2014, the Rajya Sabha on 20 February, the President gave assent on 1 March, and Telangana came into existence on 2 June 2014.

secs.t: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 → dates and Parts — Part → subject → sections

x: Exam angle: "What is covered under Part II / Part XII?" Answers: Reorganisation of the State; amendment of Articles 371D and 168.
Part II
(Sections 3-11) covers the reorganisation itself: formation of Telangana, the common capital and the common Governor (APPSC 2023 key).
The Act has 12 Parts, 108 Sections (Section 108 is the removal-of-difficulties clause) and 13 Schedules (the Thirteenth lists the institutions and infrastructure promised to AP).

secs.t: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 → Section → subject

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2023 keyed "Arrears of taxes - Section 50" as the correct match.
Section 8 assigned responsibility for law and order, internal security, vital installations and government buildings in the common capital.

Section 26 concerns delimitation; Section 46 concerns the Finance Commission award and related grants; Sections 84-85 concern the Apex Council and River Management Boards; and Section 90 concerns Polavaram.

Section 3 dealt with formation of Telangana; Section 5 with Hyderabad as common capital; Section 6 with the expert committee on a new capital for Andhra Pradesh; and Section 8 with the Governor's special responsibility for security.

secs.t: Seats, legislatures and High Court after bifurcation → data

x: Article 168
was changed in relation to the Legislative Council of Telangana.
Section 30 provided for the common High Court at Hyderabad until
a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh was established under Article 214
The judges’ salaries of the common High Court were shared according to the population ratio of Andhra Pradesh to Telangana, namely

secs.t: Division of assets and liabilities → basis; Schedules → contents — Item → basis of division

x: The residuary State of Andhra Pradesh lost Hyderabad, a major revenue-generating centre, and faced revenue deficits after bifurcation.
Power was apportioned on the basis of the average consumption during the preceding five years.
Section 56
provides for apportionment of tax refunds according to population.
The relevant bases are location for assets, population for liabilities and refunds, and place of assessment for tax arrears.

secs.t: Division of assets and liabilities → basis; Schedules → contents — Schedule → contents

x: The Ninth Schedule covers PSUs and corporations, the Tenth State institutions, the Eleventh irrigation projects, and the Twelfth coal, oil, gas and power.
The Thirteenth Schedule included institutions such as IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS, central and tribal universities, and infrastructure proposals including a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.

secs.t: AP capital → committees, Amaravati, three capitals, 2026 Act

x: The 2026 Act amended Section 5 (the capital provision).
The Srikrishna Committee reported in December 2010 with six options.
Amaravati was chosen in 2015 after land pooling involving approximately
33,000 acres
The three-capitals plan introduced in 2020 failed in court in 2022.

secs.t: Post-bifurcation disputes → rivers, Polavaram, Special Category Status

x: Section 108 empowers the Centre to remove difficulties, but it and the related expert committees do not prescribe deadlines or possess binding force.
The 2014 Amendment Ordinance amended
Section 3
and transferred seven Khammam mandals in the Polavaram submergence area to Andhra Pradesh.
The Ordinance transferred seven specified mandals and retained the Bhurgumpadu villages in Andhra Pradesh; it did not transfer the entire Khammam district.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The movement was significant for making separate statehood a major political issue, and its student-party-central formula sequence was repeated in 2001–2014.
K. Jayashankar was a former Vice-Chancellor of
Kakatiya University
and was widely regarded as the ideologue of the Telangana movement.
The two regional agitations were followed by the Six-Point Formula in 1973 and Article 371D, which provided the constitutional basis for local cadres and related arrangements.
Although the system replaced political assurances with constitutional zoning, disputes over non-local appointments continued, including issues associated with GO 610 and the Girglani Commission.
The Mulki question is traced from
and is linked with the 1969 and 1972 agitations, Article 371D, GO 610 and bifurcation.
The stated 2026 profile gives Amaravati as the capital, an area of 1,60,205 square kilometres and a coastline of 974 kilometres.

rows.title: Naxalite movement in Andhra Pradesh - Srikakulam origins, course and impact
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Uprisings → place, period, leaders, causes (Naxalbari 1967, Srikakulam 1968-70)

x: The “Ballot to Bullet” line rejected
the CPI(M)’s parliamentary path
and favoured armed revolutionary struggle.
Land concentration, failed reforms such as zamindari abolition, ceilings and tenancy reforms, and tribal exploitation were identified as causes.
Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal
led the Naxalbari uprising in Darjeeling district.
The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally dated to
, although 1968–69 is also used in some references.

secs.t: Naxalite groups → founders, years, bases (1967-2004)

x: The CPI(ML) was formed in 1969, described India as semi-feudal and followed the Chinese-model strategy of protracted guerrilla war.
CPI(ML) is associated with Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal; the AP extremist wing with the four Andhra leaders; PWG with Kondapalli Seetharamaiah; and CPI (Maoist) with the PWG–MCC merger.
The AP extremist CPI(ML) wing dates to 1967, CPI(ML) to 1969, PWG to 1980, and CPI (Maoist) to 2004.

secs.t: Literary bodies → founders and FIRSTs (Virasam, Jana Natya Mandali, 1970-71)

x: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
were the founding vice-presidents of Virasam.
Jhamjha, published in 1970, is identified as the first revolutionary poetry collection.
Sri Sri
was Virasam's founding president; the seed was a pamphlet handed out by Andhra University students at his 60th-birthday celebrations in Vizag in 1970.

secs.t: Regulations and institutions → impact on land and tribal areas

x: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation procures minor forest produce and supplies essential goods, helping free tribals from moneylenders.
The movement placed land to the tiller and tribal land alienation at the centre of politics, and Dalits within it later concentrated on land struggles.
Regulation 1 of 1970, a response to the tribal unrest, barred transfer of land in Scheduled Areas from tribals to non-tribals.

secs.t: State responses → year and key fact (1975-2014)

x: The Anandapuram Greyhounds base is credited with securing the LWE corridor in the Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts along the Odisha–Chhattisgarh borders.
The national toolkit includes intelligence-led operations, stronger state police, rehabilitation, dialogue, and development of roads and mobile towers.
The Bhargava Commission, headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava, was set up in 1977 to inquire into alleged encounter killings during the Emergency.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Srikakulam helped make Andhra Pradesh a core base of Indian Maoism and influenced Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.
H.J. Dora was DGP from 1996 to 2002, Greyhounds neutralised several top leaders, and over 1,200 cadres surrendered during 1998–2001.
The Greyhounds base at Anandapuram secures the LWE corridor of the Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) and Parvathipuram Manyam districts in north coastal Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: Social movements in Andhra Pradesh - Dalit, backward class, farmers' and anti-arrack movements
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Movements → started by, place and year

x: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in 1985 after Karamchedu, with Katti Padmarao identified as its founder and Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder.
Bhu Poratam continued the Communist tradition of tenancy and land campaigns carried out during 1956–69.
Vardhineni Rosamma
of Dubagunta was a prominent leader of the anti-arrack movement.

secs.t: Persons → contributions

x: Katti Padmarao, Manda Krishna Madiga and Endluri Sudhakar are associated with that assertion.

secs.t: Events → date and district

x: The Karamchedu massacre occurred in
Prakasam
district on 17 July 1985.
After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties and formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas.
Left parties and farmers protested electricity tariff hikes introduced under power-sector reforms during the 2000 agitation.
Police opened fire at Bashir Bagh in Hyderabad on 28 August 2000 during the power tariff agitation.

secs.t: Backward class commissions and BC list

x: The Anantharaman Commission, functioning during 1968–70,
was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories
The Muralidhar Rao Commission examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
Eighty-six castes were recognised as Backward Classes in Andhra, while Telangana had a separate list.

secs.t: Aims, methods and outcomes of the movements

x: Women discussed the effects of men's arrack drinking during Aksharajyothi adult-literacy classes, which helped initiate the agitation.
Women closed arrack shops and stopped arrack auctions, using broomsticks and chilli powder.
The anti-arrack movement began in Dubagunta (Nellore) in 1991, led by
rural women
from the Aksharajyothi literacy classes, and is regarded as one of India's most successful women-led movements.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: These movements broadened the political arena from the national-movement elite towards caste, gender and class assertion through organisations such as Mahasabhas, MRPS and women’s anti-arrack groups.
Phule’s Satyashodhak Samaj, founded in 1873, and Periyar’s Self-Respect Movement influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders.
After Mandal, divisions emerged between OBC and Dalit movements over sub-categorisation.

rows.title: Women's movement in Andhra Pradesh, 1956-2014
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Organisations and journals → founder / editor and year

x: Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded in 1937, POW in 1974, Stree Shakti Sanghatana in 1978 and Mahila Dakshata Samiti in 1990.
The first State women's Mahasabha was organised by Communist women in 1947, not 1964.
Bhumika was founded in 1993 and its editor was
Kondaveeti Satyavathi
Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s Janana and Satihita Bodhini promoted women’s education and widow remarriage.

secs.t: Women leaders → FIRSTs and contributions

x: Sharda Mukherjee became Governor in 1977; 1999 is the year Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker.
The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference, associated with Bhagya Reddy Varma, demanded abolition of the
Jogini and Devadasi systems
Muthulakshmi Reddy’s campaign was followed by Ammannaraja’s 1937 anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly.

secs.t: Acts, amendments and campaigns → year and provision

x: The Madras Act is of 1947 and the AP Devadasis Act of 1988.
NCRB recorded
about 15,000 dowry cases and 6,100 dowry deaths
The 1986 Andhra Pradesh amendment gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property, well before the Central amendment of 2005.
The Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026 was defeated in April 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The movement moved from reform bodies such as Andhra Mahila Sabha to Left and autonomous groups, then to mass action such as Anti-arrack and SHG-based economic activity.
One Stop Centres cover all 26 districts, the 181 helpline has run since 2016, there are 28 Shakti Sadans, and BBBP covers all 26 districts.

rows.title: Important cultural events between 1956 and 2014 - literature, journalism, theatre and cinema
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Cultural institutions → year and FIRSTs

x: The Sahitya Akademi was set up in 1952, Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1953, Lalit Kala Akademi in 1954, and Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in 1985.
In 1985, the NTR Government merged the State akademis into the newly established
Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University
The APPSC G2 2017 key gives
Dr S. Radhakrishnan
; an AP History PYQ book gives Jawaharlal Nehru, but the official key is followed.

secs.t: World Telugu Conferences → venue and year

x: Exam angle: the first conference year (1975) is asked repeatedly; it is also the year of the International Telugu Institute.
The First Conference was held at Hyderabad, the Second at Kuala Lumpur, the Third in Mauritius and the Fourth at Tirupati.
The Fourth World Telugu Conference was held at Tirupati in 2012, not at Vijayawada.

secs.t: Newspapers and journals → founder and year

x: Andhra Jyothi was founded by K.L.N. Prasad, Eenadu by Ramoji Rao, Udayam by Dasari Narayana Rao and Sakshi by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
Andhra Jyothi was launched in 1960, Eenadu in Visakhapatnam in 1974, and Sakshi in 2008.
Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal, and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence.

secs.t: Awards → awardees, year and prize

x: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1965 for
Misra Manjari
The Sahitya Akademi Award covers 24 languages—22 Eighth Schedule languages along with English and Rajasthani—and carries Rs 1 lakh.
Jashuva received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1964 and the Padma Bhushan in 1970.
The coalition government revived the Kandukuri Awards and announced the revival of the Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The announcements were associated with Minister Kandula Durgesh and the Undavalli Caves location.
Andhra Pradesh announced an annual Telugu Mahotsavam to revive several folk and theatre forms, and Nandi Natakotsavams are also proposed to be revived.
The festival was scheduled for 15 July 2026 at 150 locations in connection with 150 years of Vande Mataram, with two Andhra Pradesh plays selected.

rows.title: Development of Telugu literature after 1956 - Digambara, Viplava, Dalit, feminist and Muslim minority streams
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Literary movements → founded, year and FIRSTs

x: The three volumes appeared during 1965-68; 1970 is when several Digambaras moved to Virasam.
Cherabandaraju, Jwalamukhi and Nikhileswar
moved on to Virasam in 1970.
The Srikakulam peasant struggle of 1969 under Vempatapu Satyam helped spread
Naxalism
in Andhra.
The spoken-Telugu revolution associated with Gidugu and Gurajada laid the linguistic foundation on which feminist and Dalit fiction developed.

secs.t: Pen names → real names

x: Mahaswapna was the pen name of Kammisetti Venkateswara Rao.

secs.t: Poets → contributions

x: Firdausi is Jashuva’s poem about the Persian poet who was cheated of his promised reward by Sultan Mahmud.
Jayaprabha, Vimala and Kondepudi Nirmala
are among the poets associated with Neeli Meghalu.
Puttumacha, meaning ‘Birthmark’, is a long poem by
Khadar Mohiuddin
on Muslim identity.

secs.t: Books → authors and themes — Poetry

x: Maha Prasthanam
broke conventional Telugu prosody and presented a call to the oppressed.
Chikkanavutunna Pata was edited by G. Lakshmi Narasaiah and Tripuraneni Srinivas.
Gabbilam was modelled on
Kalidasa’s Meghaduta
, in which a messenger carries a message.
Nallapoddu was edited by
Gogu Syamala
(APPSC G2 2017 key; the 'Mallepoddu' version of the question has the same answer).

secs.t: Books → authors and themes — Novels

x: Exam angle: author-work matching; distractors Tulasidalam, Mahaprasthanam, Vennello Aadapilla sit beside Veyi Padagalu.
Veyi Padagalu, Athadu Adavini Jayinchadu, Ramayana Vishavruksham and Tulasidalam are associated respectively with Viswanatha Satyanarayana, Kesava Reddy, Ranganayakamma and Yandamuri Veerendranath.
Ramayana Vishavruksham by Ranganayakamma is described as a
Marxist-feminist critique of the Ramayana
P.V. Narasimha Rao
translated Veyi Padagalu into Hindi as Sahasraphan.

secs.t: Jnanpith awardees → work and year

x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana, C. Narayana Reddy and Ravuri Bharadwaja received the Jnanpith Award in 1970, 1988 and 2012 respectively.
Viswambhara is associated with C. Narayana Reddy.
Viswanatha Satyanarayana was known as ‘Abhinava Nannaya’ and wrote over 100 works.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Post-1956 Telugu literary streams broadened the subject matter of literature to include
caste, class, gender and minority identity
, moving beyond classical and romantic themes.
Digambara, Viplava, Dalit, feminist and Muslim minority streams are all identified as important post-1956 developments in Telugu literature.
Telugu is counted among India’s six classical languages and is spoken by more than
10 crore
people.

rows.title: Telugu cinema and mass culture in Andhra Pradesh
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: FIRSTs of Telugu cinema

x: Bhishma Pratigna was released in 1921, Bhakta Prahlada in 1931 and Lava Kusa in 1963.
Lava Kusa was directed by C. Pullaiah and C.S. Rao; H.M. Reddy made Bhakta Prahlada and Gruha Lakshmi.
The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is presented by the President along with the
National Film Awards
The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969, and Devika Rani was its first recipient.

secs.t: Film personalities → contributions

x: B.N. Reddy
was known for social and lyrical films, including Malliswari.
Pathala Bhairavi is associated with K.V. Reddy, not K. Viswanath.
N.T. Rama Rao’s portrayals of Rama and Krishna in mythological films built his
mass image
Sowcar Janaki made her debut in
Shavukaru
in 1950, directed by L.V. Prasad.
Bapu made films in association with
Mullapudi Venkata Ramana

secs.t: Film studios → founder, place and year

x: Vijaya Vauhini Studios was founded by B.
Nagi Reddy and Aluri Chakrapani
Ramanaidu
Studios was founded by D. Ramanaidu.
Guinness lists Ramoji Film City as the world’s largest
film studio complex
The industry’s post-1956 movement from Madras to Hyderabad helped build the
Hyderabad studio belt
Annapurna Studios (Hyderabad, 1970s) was founded by Akkineni Nageswara Rao.

secs.t: Film awards → awardees and year

x: The correct order is B.N. Reddy (1974), Akkineni Nageswara Rao (1990), D. Ramanaidu (2009), and K. Viswanath (2016).
Anant Nag is the second Kannada actor after Rajkumar to receive it.
The Nandi Awards cover
films, television and drama
, including Nandi Natakotsavam for drama.
The Nandi Awards lapsed under the previous government, and their revival was announced in 2026.

secs.t: Actors turned politicians → party and post

x: The Praja Rajyam Party merged with the Congress in 2011, not the TDP.
K. Pawan Kalyan is associated with the Jana Sena Party and became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
The Telugu Desam Party’s slogan was
Telugu Vari Atma Gauravam
The TDP was founded when
Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy
was Chief Minister (APPSC Group 2, 2019).

secs.t: Television and mass media → year

x: Doordarshan Kendra Hyderabad was established in 1977.
ETV was founded by Ramoji Rao.
Prasar Bharati comprises
Akashvani
and Doordarshan.
The National Film Awards are administered by the
National Film Development Corporation
, or NFDC.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Telugu cinema also influenced mass politics, especially through N.T. Rama Rao and the TDP.
N.T. Rama Rao became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 1983.
Anant Nag was named the awardee for 2024 and became the second Kannada actor after Rajkumar to receive the award.
Nandi Natakotsavam is the
drama
-related component of the Nandi Awards framework.

rows.title: Art, architecture and archaeology in Andhra Pradesh after 1956; museums and heritage
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-215

secs.t: Modern painters → titles, styles and pen names

x: Exam angle: the "Father of Modern Contemporary Art" PYQ lists Bapiraju, Papaiah and Bapu as distractors.
Damerla Rama Rao was a pioneer of modern Andhra painting associated with
Rajahmundry
, where an art gallery named after him is located.
Bapu was known for his line drawings of epic characters, worked as an illustrator and film director, and received the Telugu Velugu award for painting in Ugadi 2012.

secs.t: Heritage bodies and laws → year and founder

x: The AMASR (Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains) Act is of 1958.
The department traces its origin to the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department established in 1914.
The Commissioner’s office of the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums is located at
Vijayawada
The ASI was founded in 1861 by Alexander Cunningham.

secs.t: Sites → excavator and finds

x: Salihundam was discovered by Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy; A. Ranganatha Saraswati found Nagarjunakonda in 1926.
Salihundam
in Srikakulam was a Mahayana–Vajrayana port known for Tara bronzes and a Buddha footprint.
The monuments dismantled and rebuilt on higher ground because of Nagarjunasagar Dam submergence are called
Transplanted Monuments
Ravindra Bharathi auditorium in Hyderabad was constructed in 1961 as part of the observance of the Tagore centenary.

secs.t: Museums → location and collections

x: The Salar Jung Museum at Hyderabad contains the collection of Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, also known as Salar Jung III, gathered over more than 40 years.
The
Nagarjunakonda island museum
, located in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir, houses archaeological material rescued from the submerged area, including Ikshvaku-Buddhist finds.
Veiled Rebecca was bought in Rome in 1876 and is in the Salar Jung Museum.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Archaeological Survey of India began scientific conservation of the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple at Mangalagiri.
The
division of museum antiques
remained one of the unfinished items arising from the 2014 bifurcation.
Cosmetic restoration is criticised for failing to protect the authentic historical character of heritage sites.

rows.title: Post-independence consolidation - land reforms, tribal and border policy, national integration
sub: Group-II M1-A-115: Important social events between 1956 and 2014 - reform, welfare and legislation

secs.t: Land reforms — phases, types and FIRSTs

x: The first phase covered 1947–70, the second began in 1970, and the Kumarappa Committee of 1949 set the reform agenda.
Abolition of intermediaries
was regarded as the most successful reform and brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State.
Land consolidation achieved notable success in
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh

secs.t: Committees and persons → contributions

x: Raj Krishna classified land reforms as
liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental
A Philosophy for NEFA argued for cultural autonomy and limitations on the alienation of tribal land.
The formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin under the influence of Jawaharlal Nehru.
The
Naga National Council
, associated with A.Z. Phizo, demanded independence for the Naga areas.

secs.t: Abolition of intermediaries → Act and year

x: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in 1949 to abolish intermediaries in Telangana.
The Andhra Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was enacted in 1956.
Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after the abolition measures.
The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act is of 1948 (APP gives 1949, in force 1950).

secs.t: Tenancy and ceiling laws → year and provision — Laws and ministries

x: The AP Andhra Area Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the
Subba Rao Committee
The Act required written lease deeds, prescribed leases of at least six years and came into force in 1961.
The 1961 ceiling law was weakened by
benami transfers and exemptions
The Act is of 1973 (PYQ) and followed the Land Reforms Bill under CM P.V. Narasimha Rao (1971-73).

secs.t: Tenancy and ceiling laws → year and provision — Key provisions

x: The maximum retainable area was 54 acres of ‘K’ grade, the lowest-grade, land.

secs.t: Bhoodan and Gramdan → founder, village and state

x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave began the Bhoodan Movement at
Pochampalli
on 18 April 1951.
Pochampalli was in Nalgonda district of Hyderabad State (now Telangana).
Gramdan was the next stage of Bhoodan in which an entire village was gifted to the community.

secs.t: Tribal policy → principles and provisions

x: Nehru rejected both the museum approach of isolation and forced assimilation, favouring integration while respecting tribal identity and institutions.
Statements 1, 2 and 3 express the Tribal Panchsheel.
PESA 1996 applies to Scheduled Areas in states covered by the Fifth Schedule; it does not apply to the Sixth Schedule autonomous district areas.

secs.t: Border consolidation → how and when

x: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated through Operation Vijay, while Pondicherry was a French enclave.
NEFA was run through the
Governor of Assam
and served as a policy laboratory for Elwin's approach.
Pondicherry was transferred in 1954, Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated in 1961, Pondicherry became a Union Territory in 1962, and Goa attained statehood in 1987.

secs.t: National integration → body and year

x: The National Integration Council was established by Nehru in 1961 after the
National Integration Conference
The conference considered
communalism, casteism, regionalism and linguism
as threats to national integration.
The State's tools against regionalism are the National Integration Council, Article 44, Article 51A and the Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules.
The relevant anti-Hindi agitations occurred in 1937, 1965 and 1986.

secs.t: AP social legislation and reservation → year

x: N.T. Rama Rao
imposed total prohibition in 1995, after the 1993 arrack ban under Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy.
Backward Muslims got 4% under BC-E. Statement 2 is wrong: the 4% reservation came in 2007; 1986 was when NTR raised the BC quota to 44%.
The
Muralidhar Rao Commission
(1982) led to NTR raising the BC quota to 44% in 1986, later struck down by the High Court.

secs.t: AP welfare schemes and universities → CM and year

x: The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme, along with subsidised housing and Janata cloth, was associated with N.T. Rama Rao and introduced in 1983.
The
Fee Reimbursement
scheme, introduced in 2008, supported higher education for poor students and was associated with Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
The Andhra Pradesh Open University, now named Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University, was the first open university in India and was established in 1982.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Tana Bhagats cited the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, or PESA, and the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.
Oral leases, benami transfers and exemptions were all identified as practices that weakened the implementation of tenancy and ceiling laws.
The Eluru agency land dispute involves
APSALT Regulation 1/59 and Regulation 1/70
, showing that tribal land law remains subject to litigation.

rows.title: Tribal culture of Andhra - major tribes, social organisation, festivals, dances and art forms
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I A-216

secs.t: Tribe — definition and constitutional process

x: Marshall Sahlins
described a tribe as a segmental organisation of equivalent multi-family groups.
The President notifies after consulting the Governor.

secs.t: Social organisation → terms and village offices

x: The Chenchus are an endogamous tribe with exogamous clans or kulams/gothrams; their organisation is patriarchal and patrilineal.
Raju is associated with the Bhoomani clan.
The three village office holders come from different clans and officiate marriages in each Chenchu village.
Ghotul is the example of a youth dormitory associated with the
Muria
of Chhattisgarh.

secs.t: Economy, art and crafts → tribe

x: Idital wall paintings are associated with the Savara, also known as Sora, community.
Warli art belongs to Maharashtra.
Pithora is associated with the Rathwa community of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
The agency economy includes podu or shifting cultivation, minor forest produce, and coffee and horticulture in the Araku belt.

secs.t: Festivals → tribe

x: Eetela Panduga or Chaitrapurab is
the spring festival of the Araku tribes
, during which Dhimsa is danced.
Seethala Panduga
is a Lambadi festival observed in Ashada.
All four statements correctly describe the stated Lambadi festivals, their occasions and associated terminology.
Modakondamma is regarded as the goddess of the
Paderu agency
, where an annual tribal jatara is held.

secs.t: Dances → tribe

x: The instruments associated with Dhimsa include dappu, tudumu, mori, kidgi, gilka and jodukommulu.
The stated regional association of Dhimsa is with the Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam areas.
Koya performers of the Kommu dance are associated with
bison-horn headgear
Dhimsa is danced by the
Bagata, Gadaba, Kondadora, Poraja and Valmiki
(other sources add Savara, Jatapu, Khond and Kotia).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Tribes Art Fest presented more than 1,000 works representing over 30 traditions at Travancore Palace, New Delhi.
Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion in the Eastern Ghats from 1922 to 1924.

All four statements reflect the stated comparative profile: STs formed 8.6% of India’s population, Bhil was the largest tribe, Gond the second-largest, and Madhya Pradesh had the largest tribal population.
